Case_12006/figure2.jpg.source_caption: CT of the chest. Arrows indicate chest tube placement.

description.short_caption: CT of the chest showing bilateral chest tubes and extensive lung abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates bilateral chest tubes, indicated by arrows, positioned in the pleural spaces. The lung parenchyma shows extensive abnormalities, including areas of consolidation, cavitation, and possible air-fluid levels, suggestive of severe infectious or inflammatory processes. The mediastinum appears midline, and no significant pleural effusion is evident. The image is in a lung window setting, optimizing visualization of pulmonary structures.
visible_findings: bilateral chest tubes in pleural spaces

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary opacities and medical devices.
description.detailed_description: This is an anteroposterior chest radiograph showing the thorax. Bilateral pulmonary opacities are visible, more pronounced in the lower lung zones, suggesting possible consolidation or infiltrates. Several medical devices, including ECG leads, are present on the chest wall. The cardiac silhouette appears within normal limits, and there is no visible pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

Case_12006/figure4.jpg.source_caption: H and E stain of lung tissue, 200x magnification.

description.short_caption: H&E stain of lung tissue showing inflammation and cellular infiltrates.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows lung tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) at 200x magnification. The tissue demonstrates prominent inflammatory infiltrates composed of numerous lymphocytes and plasma cells, along with some multinucleated giant cells. Alveolar spaces appear disrupted, with evidence of cellular debris and congestion. The findings suggest an infectious or inflammatory process within the lung parenchyma.
visible_findings: inflammatory infiltrates with lymphocytes and plasma cells

description.short_caption: Axial CT of the chest showing bilateral lung abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates bilateral lung abnormalities. There are multiple cavitary lesions visible in both lungs, with surrounding areas of ground-glass opacities. The mediastinum and heart are centrally located, and no significant pleural effusion is noted. The findings are suggestive of an infectious or inflammatory process.
visible_findings: bilateral cavitary lesions in the lungs

Case_12006/figure6.jpg.source_caption: CMV immunoperoxidase stain of lung tissue, 400x magnification.

description.short_caption: CMV immunoperoxidase stain of lung tissue showing viral inclusions, 400x magnification.
description.detailed_description: This image shows lung tissue stained with an immunoperoxidase technique to highlight cytomegalovirus (CMV) antigens. At 400x magnification, large, dark brown-stained inclusions are visible within some cells, consistent with CMV infection. The background tissue is counterstained in a lighter blue, allowing clear visualization of the infected cells amidst the surrounding lung parenchyma.

Case_12006/figure5.jpg.source_caption: H and E stain of lung tissue, 400x magnification.

description.short_caption: H&E stain of lung tissue showing granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows lung tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) at high magnification (approximately 400x). The tissue exhibits granulomatous inflammation characterized by clusters of epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleated giant cells. Surrounding the granuloma are numerous lymphocytes and scattered plasma cells. The presence of multinucleated giant cells suggests a chronic inflammatory process, potentially related to an infectious or non-infectious etiology.
